name.text: Using Trig ratios to Find the Vertical Side

questiontext.text:
Solve for \(x\). Do not convert your answer to decimal form. Rationalize and simplify if needed.

Hint: To type trig expressions in your work:

  • Use sin (x ), cos(x) , tan (x) for sine, cosine, and tangent. Example: sin (30) → \(\sin 30 \)

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-2, 12, 12, -2], axis: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); /* Right-angle triangle coordinates */ const A = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // right angle const B = board.create('point', [10, 0], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // bottom right (angle theta) const C = board.create('point', [0, 10], {name: '', fixed: true, size: 2}); // top (length x) /* Triangle edges */ board.create('segment', [A, B]); board.create('segment', [A, C]); board.create('segment', [B, C]); /* Right-angle square at A */ board.create('polygon', [ board.create('point', [0, 0], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [1, 0], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [1, 1], {visible:false}), board.create('point', [0, 1], {visible:false}) ], { fillColor: 'white', fillOpacity: 1, borders: {strokeColor: 'black'} }); /* Labels */ board.create('text', [-0.5, 5, 'x'], {fontSize: 14}); // vertical side board.create('text', [5, 6, '{#hyp#}'], {fontSize: 14}); // hypotenuse (random) board.create('text', [8, 0.5, '{#theta#}°'], {fontSize: 14}); // angle at B (random) [[/jsxgraph]]

We have a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left, hypotenuse {@h@}, and an angle {@theta@}° at the bottom-right. We need to find the vertical side x.

The vertical side opposite the angle is related to the hypotenuse by the sine ratio:

\[ \sin({@theta@}°) = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{x}{@h@} \]

Solving for x gives:

\[ x = {@h@} \,\sin({@theta@}°) \]

Evaluate exactly (no decimals):

  • \(\sin 30° = \tfrac{1}{2}\)
  • \(\sin 45° = \tfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\),
  • \(\sin 60° = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)
  • For other angles (e.g. 35°, 40°, 55°), leave the answer as the exact trig expression: \[ x = {@h@} \,\sin({@theta@}°) \] Replace \(\sin({@theta@}°)\) with a known exact value if possible.

Tips:

  • When the sine involves a square root, write the answer as \(\frac{{@h@}\sqrt{n}}{2}\), not with a root in the denominator.
  • Always rationalise the denominator if needed.
  • Keep answers exact — do not convert to decimals.

Example: If we have hypoteneus as 8 \( \theta\) = 60°:

then \( x = 8\sin 60° = 8 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 4\sqrt{3}. \)
